entries.title: Psalms 86:1
segments:
. This is a prayer in which the writer, with deep emotion, mingles petitions and praises, now urgent for help, and now elated with hope, in view of former mercies. The occurrence of many terms and phrases peculiar to David's Psalms clearly intimates its authorship.

segments: 13, 14. The reason: God had delivered him from death and the power of insolent, violent, and godless persecutors (

entries.title: Psalms 86:17
segments: 17. Show me--literally, "Make with me a token," by Thy providential care. Thus in and by his prosperity his enemies would be confounded.
